text:
sasha: Drafting the benchmark narrative for next week's launch. Core ask: a crisp latency + cost story that scales from hosted to dedicated. Need charts, a 2-3 line headline, and a short social post. Who can validate numbers?

miguel: Love this. Who's the audience — infra buyers or engineering teams? That will change the framing (SLOs vs $/token).

sasha: Primary audience = engineers/infra leads evaluating inference platforms. Secondary = product leaders who care about unit economics. So prioritize SLO language but make cost an easy, headlineable metric.

anya: Chart suggestions: 1) P50/P95 latency vs throughput (requests/sec) for our default model vs compressed variants, 2) cost per 1M tokens normalized (hosted vs dedicated vs open-hosted competitor), 3) tail-latency distribution heatmap. Keep labels simple.

anya: For headline: "Same latency SLO, up to 2x lower inference cost" — is that defensible?

miguel: We should avoid absolute multipliers unless eng sign-off. Maybe: "Cut per-token inference cost—without sacrificing latency" as a safe first pass.

tom: I can run a quick sweep to validate numbers. What models, sequence lengths, and quantization settings should I test?

sasha: Good Q. Start with: - model: redwood-4b-v1 (FP16) and redwood-4b-q8 (8-bit) - sequence lengths: 64 / 256 / 1024 - batch sizes: 1, 8, 32 - metric: p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec; cost = (GPU cost pro-rated + infra overhead) / tokens.

tom: Ok running now. Posting raw CSV to the sheet when done. ETA ~45m.

benchbot: Auto-update: Benchmark run queued by tom. Tracker: https://redwood.share/bench-sweeps/2024-launch (view-only). Results will be posted to the sheet in this thread. :gear:

olivia: From GTM: we'll need the headline and one-line value prop for the landing page, plus 3 bullet talking points for the webinar. Also please add UTM params for inbound routing: utm_campaign=bench_launch_2024&utm_source=organic_social. SDR routing rule: tag leads as "bench_webinar" and assign to team "growth-sdr".

sasha: Draft landing blurb: "Redwood Inference: predictable latency, dramatically lower per-token costs — production-ready inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Shorten if needed.

miguel: For charts, recommend visual emphasis on P95 lines and a small callout box with cost-per-100k-tokens numbers. Use color palette consistent with the product site.

anya: Also propose a one-slide explainer of the tech levers: batching, KV caching, quantization, and smart routing — each with a 1-line customer benefit. That helps position vs competitors who only tout raw throughput.

benchbot: Upload complete: CSV results posted to sheet (link above). Summary: redwood-4b-q8 shows ~1.8x lower infra cost at matched P95 vs redwood-4b-fp16 for seq=256, batch=8. Raw numbers in sheet.

tom: Verified numbers in sheet. FYI the 1.8x is for our lab pricing model; enterprise dedicated unit economics differ (better for higher sustained throughput). Will add a footnote.

sasha: Great. Let's bake that into the narrative: "Lab results: up to 1.8x lower infra cost at matched P95 for common chat workloads (256 tokens). Dedicated customers can expect greater savings at sustained throughput."

olivia: That wording works. For the webinar CTA, we want: "Sign up to see a live demo and get a personalized cost estimate." Can we add a short form field for average tokens/min so we can route qualified leads?

miguel: Suggest adding a competitor comparison row in the slide deck (no logos, just "Generic Cloud A" / "Other API" labels) showing lower unit cost at typical latencies. Avoid naming real vendors.

anya: For the social copy (thread + blog): "New: benchmarked inference that balances latency and cost. See live demos + a free estimate for your workload. Link ->" + landing URL. Keep it under 220 characters for X.

olivia: SDRs: please tag leads with channel and add lead notes indicating whether they requested a dedicated estimate. Routing confirmed: growth-sdr queue, triage by region.

tom: Quick technical note for the marketing deck: include the test command we ran so reviewers can reproduce.

tom: ```bash
# run perf sweep
python perf/sweep.py --model redwood-4b --quant q8,fp16 --seq 64,256,1024 --batch 1,8,32 --out results.csv
```

anya: Nice. Also include visualization config so design can reproduce: x-axis = throughput (req/sec), y-axis = latency (ms), separate series per model/quant. Cost inset = bar chart (cost per 100k tokens).

benchbot: FYI: preliminary slide export uploaded: https://redwood.share/slides/bench-launch-draft. Feedback thread on slides enabled.

sasha: Next steps: 1) Tom finalize verified numbers + footnotes (today) 2) Design produce 3 final chart variations (P95 focus, cost focus, compact social tile) (EOD tomorrow) 3) Draft blog + X thread + webinar landing copy (olivia + anya) (first drafts tomorrow morning) 4) Set up tracking & SDR routing (olivia) 5) Dry run for webinar with demo (sasha + tom) next Wed.

olivia: I'll set up the landing page and UTM links today and confirm routing.

miguel: I'll review the draft blog for technical accuracy.

anya: I'll iterate copy for the slide callouts and short-form social.

sasha: Thanks all — if anyone sees a risky claim, flag it here. Otherwise we'll ship the first draft to the company for feedback at 1700PT tomorrow. :rocket:
